openQuestions.q: command-policy.ts:330 marks story_dispatch as status:'supported' (not 'legacy'), yet plan.md CHK-005 and decision.json rationale treat it as a deprecated alias removable alongside finding_dispatch. The cli-engine-english-open-source-execution-plan.md manifest rows M593-M598 show B-9d95 CHK-004 merged story_dispatch/finding_dispatch into lattice dispatch, treating both as superseded. However only finding_dispatch has status:'legacy' in the policy file; story_dispatch retains status:'supported'. Plan calls this a stale mislabel and removes it directly. Is removing story_dispatch (status:supported) in this story correct — confirmed dead with no active consumers — or is this a contradiction that needs explicit acknowledgment that the supported label was never accurate post-B-9d95?
openQuestions.evidence: packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:330 story_dispatch: { status: 'supported', ownershipClass: 'readOnly', allowedPhases: ['DEV'], ... }. command-policy.ts:331 finding_dispatch: { status: 'legacy', ... replacement: 'Use lattice dispatch with itemId, findingId, or clusterId.' }. plan.md CHK-005: 'story_dispatch status:supported is a stale mislabel; both are deprecated and removed together'. decision.json rationale: 'story_dispatch/finding_dispatch are both confirmed deprecated by cli-engine-english-open-source-execution-plan.md (B-9d95 CHK-004 merged both into lattice dispatch); the command-policy story_dispatch status:supported is a stale mislabel deleted alongside the alias.'
openQuestions.resolution: story_dispatch is confirmed dead and removable. The command-policy.ts:330 status:supported is a stale mislabel (asymmetric with finding_dispatch:331 status:legacy). Authoritative: cli-engine-english-open-source-execution-plan.md (B-9d95 CHK-004, M593-M598) records story_dispatch + finding_dispatch were merged into the unified lattice dispatch; the handler at story-dispatch.ts:469 already prints "story_dispatch will be removed in versions after B-9d95, please switch to lattice dispatch". Grep confirms NO active consumer of the story_dispatch CLI alias: only the registry def (cli-engine:1901), the policy entry (:330), the deprecation-warning handler method (story-dispatch.ts:463), and the process-fact-levels.ts:267 inventory entry — zero test assertions, and the dispatch() clusterId branch uses cluster.ts finding_dispatch (a different function). CHK-005 therefore removes both CLI aliases + their command-policy entries + the process-fact-levels inventory entries together, correcting the mislabel by deletion.

openQuestions.q: decisions/koala-to-lattice-role-naming-execution-plan.md (B-ffa2) line 99 states as an explicit non-goal: 'Do not rename .koala/ runtime directories, locks, dispatches, activity logs, audit config, traces, or artifact registry entries as part of the role-ID rename. .koala path migration is a separate storage/runtime compatibility project.' CHK-001 of this story removes the .koala read FALLBACK from active source (LEGACY_KOALA_DIR + ~6 consumer files). CHK-004 updates CLAUDE.md .koala/ runtime-path doc references. Is this story the authorized successor '.koala path migration project' that B-ffa2 deferred to, or is removing the .koala read fallback in conflict with that non-goal? The story description implies it is the successor ('the runtime path is ALREADY .lattice/ for all writes; .koala/ only survives as a backward-compat READ fallback... removing the .koala read fallback is safe'), but the decisions doc does not explicitly name this story as the authorized successor.
openQuestions.evidence: koala-to-lattice-role-naming-execution-plan.md lines 99-101: 'Do not rename .koala/ runtime directories, locks, dispatches, activity logs, audit config, traces, or artifact registry entries as part of the role-ID rename. .koala path migration is a separate storage/runtime compatibility project.' Story B-a4e3 description: 'The runtime path is ALREADY .lattice/ for all writes; .koala/ only survives as a backward-compat READ fallback (LEGACY_KOALA_DIR in core/lattice-paths.ts, used in ~6 files)... So removing the .koala read fallback is safe.'
openQuestions.resolution: B-a4e3 IS the authorized successor to do the .koala path migration; no contradiction. The B-ffa2 non-goal at koala-to-lattice-role-naming-execution-plan.md:99-102 scopes itself explicitly "as part of the role-ID rename" and states ".koala path migration is a separate storage/runtime compatibility project" — i.e. it defers, not forbids. Line 97-98 of the same doc confirms compatibility contracts hold "unless a later story explicitly migrates them." B-a4e3 is that later/separate story: the .koala->.lattice WRITE migration is already complete (core/lattice-paths.ts: LATTICE_DIR=.lattice canonical, LEGACY_KOALA_DIR=.koala read-fallback only), and ~/.koala/dev-memory is already migrated to ~/.lattice with zero local .koala in this repo. CHK-001 (remove the now-dead READ fallback) and CHK-004 (reconcile CLAUDE.md .koala/ doc refs to the .lattice/ code reality) are precisely the storage/runtime compatibility finish that B-ffa2 deferred. CHK-004 only touches .koala/<dir> doc references, NOT .koala-serve.json (which the code still writes) and NOT KOALA_* env vars (explicitly excluded in scope_boundary).
